questions.sub_skill: Create and configure a file share in Azure Files
questions.prompt: You're creating a new Azure file share and have no specific reason to choose otherwise. Which billing model does Microsoft recommend?
questions.explanation: Microsoft recommends the provisioned v2 model for all new Azure Files deployments: you provision storage, IOPS and throughput independently.
why_not: Microsoft recommends provisioned v2 unless you have a specific reason for pay-as-you-go.
Microsoft recommends v2 unless you have a specific reason for v1.
Cool suits rarely accessed data; it isn't the general recommendation for new deployments.

questions.sub_skill: Create and configure a file share in Azure Files
questions.prompt: A pay-as-you-go file share is about to receive a large migration with millions of small writes. Which access tier should it start in?
questions.explanation: Transaction optimized has the lowest transaction prices. Microsoft suggests creating the share there for migration, then re-evaluating.
why_not: Cool has the highest transaction prices, the worst choice for a write-heavy migration.
Hot has higher transaction prices than transaction optimized.
Azure Files pay-as-you-go tiers are transaction optimized, hot and cool; there's no archive tier.

questions.sub_skill: Create and configure a container in Azure Blob Storage
questions.prompt: Anonymous users must be able to list the blobs in a container and read them. The account allows anonymous blob access. Which container access level do you set?
questions.explanation: The Container level allows anonymous read of blobs and of the container's listing. Blob allows blob reads only.
why_not: Blob allows anonymous reads of blobs but not listing the container.
Private allows no anonymous access.
Hot is an access tier, not an access level.

questions.sub_skill: Create and configure a container in Azure Blob Storage
questions.prompt: Which is a valid blob container name?
questions.explanation: Container names are 3-63 characters of lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, starting with a letter or number.
why_not: Container names can't contain uppercase letters or underscores.
Container names must be at least 3 characters.
Consecutive hyphens aren't allowed.

questions.prompt: Compliance data must be kept for seven years, is almost never read, and retrieval within several hours is acceptable. The account is LRS. Which tier minimises storage cost?
questions.explanation: Archive has the lowest storage cost, is offline, and suits data that can wait hours to be read. LRS accounts support it.
why_not: Cold is online and costs more per GB than archive; immediate access isn't needed.
Cool costs more per GB than cold and archive.
Hot has the highest storage cost.

questions.prompt: You must read an archived 2 GB blob urgently, but not pay an early-deletion fee, because it was archived only 40 days ago. What should you do?
options: Copy the blob to a new blob in the hot tier with High rehydration priority
Set the blob's tier to Hot with High priority
Create a lifecycle rule to move it to hot
questions.explanation: Copy Blob to a new name leaves the source in archive, so no early-deletion fee applies. High priority can complete in under an hour for blobs under 10 GB.
why_not: Changing the archived blob's tier before 180 days incurs the early-deletion fee.
Lifecycle management can't rehydrate archived blobs.
Archived blobs are offline and can't be read until rehydrated.

questions.sub_skill: Configure soft delete for blobs and containers
questions.prompt: Blob soft delete is enabled with 14 days' retention. A user deletes the whole container projects. What happens?
options: You can undelete the container for 14 days
Each blob can be undeleted individually for 14 days
The container is locked and can't be deleted
The container and its blobs are gone; blob soft delete doesn't restore containers, only container soft delete does
questions.explanation: Microsoft notes that restoring a container and its contents requires container soft delete to be enabled as well.
why_not: Blob soft delete protects individual blobs, not containers.
Deleting the container removes its blobs; blob soft delete doesn't cover container deletion.
Soft delete doesn't prevent deletion.

questions.sub_skill: Configure soft delete for blobs and containers
questions.prompt: Container soft delete is on. Container billing was deleted, and a script immediately created a new empty container named billing. What is true?
options: You can restore it under a different name
You can't restore the soft-deleted container while a container with its original name exists
The two containers are merged on restore
The new container is automatically replaced by the old one
questions.explanation: A soft-deleted container must be restored under its original name. If a new container with that name has been created, the old one can't be restored.
why_not: Containers must be restored to their original name.
There's no merge; the name conflict prevents the restore.
Nothing is replaced automatically.

questions.sub_skill: Configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files
questions.prompt: A user deleted one folder from an Azure file share. Share soft delete is enabled, and nightly share snapshots exist. How do you recover the folder?
options: Undelete it with share soft delete
Restore it from a share snapshot
questions.explanation: Share snapshots are read-only point-in-time copies from which you can restore individual files and folders, in the portal or with File Explorer Previous Versions.
why_not: Share soft delete works only at share level; it restores deleted shares, not files or folders.
Versioning applies to blobs, not Azure Files.
That's a Blob Storage feature, not Azure Files.

questions.sub_skill: Configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files
questions.prompt: A nightly job takes a share snapshot. One night it fails with error 409. What is the most likely cause?
options: The share already has 200 snapshots, the maximum
The share is in the transaction optimized tier
Snapshots only work on NFS shares
questions.explanation: Azure Files supports up to 200 snapshots per share. Creating more returns 409 until older snapshots are deleted.
why_not: Soft delete doesn't block snapshots.
Every tier supports snapshots.
Snapshots work for SMB and NFS shares.

questions.prompt: A lifecycle rule moves blobs to archive 90 days after modification. An administrator rehydrates one to hot, and the next day it's back in archive. How do you prevent this in the rule?
options: Set the rule to run weekly
Add daysAfterLastTierChangeGreaterThan to the tierToArchive action
questions.explanation: Rehydration doesn't update the last-modified time, so the archive rule matches again. daysAfterLastTierChangeGreaterThan keeps rehydrated blobs online for a minimum period.
why_not: It changes nothing for a rule based on modification time.
Lifecycle policies run once a day; you can't change the schedule.
That moves cool blobs to hot on access; it doesn't stop re-archiving.

questions.prompt: You need blobs that haven't been READ for 60 days to move to cool automatically. What must be configured?
options: Access time tracking on the account, and a rule using daysAfterLastAccessTimeGreaterThan
questions.explanation: daysAfterLastAccessTimeGreaterThan uses the LastAccessTime property, which is maintained only when access time tracking is enabled.
why_not: Modification time doesn't reflect reads.
Versioning doesn't record access times.
Creation time doesn't reflect reads either.

questions.prompt: Blob versioning and soft delete are enabled. A blob is deleted. An administrator clicks Undelete, but the blob still has no current version. What should they do?
options: Promote a previous version to current (Make current version, or copy the version over the base blob)
Wait for the soft delete retention to finish
questions.explanation: With versioning enabled, deleting a blob makes the current version a previous version. Undelete restores soft-deleted versions but not the current one; you promote a previous version.
why_not: That would permanently delete soft-deleted versions, not restore anything.
Disabling versioning doesn't restore the current version.
Rehydration applies to the archive tier, not deleted blobs.

questions.prompt: After enabling blob versioning on a busy account, storage costs grow every week. What is the recommended way to control them?
options: A lifecycle rule that deletes previous versions after a set number of days
Reduce the container soft delete retention
questions.explanation: Versions are kept until explicitly deleted. Lifecycle management can delete previous versions by age.
why_not: Soft delete isn't what's accumulating; versions are kept until deleted.
Redundancy doesn't reduce the number of stored versions.
That doesn't affect blob versions.
